caption:
Leads don't die from a bad pitch.

They die in the gap between "somebody should follow up" and nobody actually owning it.

Four steps to close that gap this week:

1. Map every stage a lead moves through, from new lead to won or lost.
2. Name one person next to each stage. Not a team. One name.
3. Set a max dwell time per stage. Five minutes for first contact. Three days before a quote gets a follow-up touch.
4. Build the escalation. Past the deadline, the lead reassigns itself or alerts a manager.

Most service businesses take hours, not minutes, to make first contact with a new lead. The ones that respond fast aren't better at sales. They assigned an owner.
